checkpoint: ROADMAP ITEM 4 §5 — runner sub-step ordering and departure seam selection

seasonalTickSubSteps.name: per-band decision loop (evaluateBandDecision + applyBandDecision)
seasonalTickSubSteps.note: iterates a bandOrder SNAPSHOT taken before the loop

seasonalTickSubSteps.name: buildTickContextCache (post-decision)
seasonalTickSubSteps.note: this cache feeds every ecology step below

seasonalTickSubSteps.name: updateBandsDemographyAndFission
seasonalTickSubSteps.note: THE CHOSEN SEAM. Iterates its own bandOrder SNAPSHOT taken at entry

seasonalTickSubSteps.name: updateBandViabilityStates
seasonalTickSubSteps.note: enumerates world.bands live — sees a band created at step 8. This is the reader that must be blocked

seasonalTickSubSteps.name: advanceTileDepletion / Fauna / Plant / Forest
seasonalTickSubSteps.note: consume the step-5 cache, so a band created at step 8 exerts no depletion this tick

seasonalTickSubSteps.name: deriveFinalReadModelContext + updateBandContextStates
seasonalTickSubSteps.note: partial rebuild when the active band set changed, so the successor enters the read model this tick

chosenSeam.why: Both the decision loop's bandOrder and updateBandsDemographyAndFission's own bandOrder are snapshots taken before their loops begin, so a band created at step 8 is in NEITHER. It therefore cannot receive a decision this tick (no free movement, no double movement) and cannot receive a demographic update this tick (no double update). It gets its first of each on the next tick, exactly once. This is also exactly where the legacy path already sits.
chosenSeam.acceptedConsequence: The ecology steps consume the step-5 cache, so the successor exerts no depletion on its birth tick. This is IDENTICAL to what the legacy daughter does today, so it is a preserved property rather than a new defect.

rejectedSeams.why: bands physically move here, so a successor created mid-loop could be handed a decision and move on its birth day — free movement
after the ecology advance the successor would miss viability and the read-model pass, appearing only in the next tick's cache — a one-tick disappearance from physical presence

rejectedSeams.name: runDailyActions
rejectedSeams.why: wrong cadence entirely; fission is annual and a daily writer would need its own resolution bound

doubleProcessingRisks.consumedTwice: prevented — the successor is not in step 4's snapshot
doubleProcessingRisks.noConsumption: accepted for the birth tick, identical to the legacy daughter
doubleProcessingRisks.twoDemographicUpdates: prevented — the successor is not in step 8's snapshot
doubleProcessingRisks.movedForFree: prevented — no decision is evaluated for it this tick
doubleProcessingRisks.duplicateReceipts: prevented — seasonalFoodReceipts is reset to undefined at construction
doubleProcessingRisks.absentFromPresence: prevented — step 12 rebuilds the read model with the changed band set
doubleProcessingRisks.ownedByBoth: prevented — the attempt resolves to the terminal `departed` phase, so hasCurrentFissionAttempt reads false

stillOpen.viabilityCleanup: step 9 enumerates world.bands live and WILL see the successor. It is listed `blocked` in PROVISIONAL_READER_MATRIX.md and is NOT yet migrated. Until it is, a production-reachable successor could be removed by Item 6 cleanup — which is one of the reasons this seam is deliberately not connected to natural fission.
